key_insight: A PINN-based, solver-agnostic training strategy can learn turbulence closures that generalize across bluff-body shapes, with the direct force model giving the strongest out-of-sample performance.
engineering_relevance: This offers a faster path to robust RANS turbulence modeling for new geometries, reducing dependence on solver-specific inverse calibration and enabling practical training from limited PIV or DNS data.
method: Train closures by imposing the RANS residual inside a PINN via automatic differentiation.
Compare four closure forms: local stress basis, non-local stress with transported turbulent kinetic energy, learned-length-scale stress, and direct force closure.
Improve deployment stability with input-gradient smoothing and a Lipschitz constraint before freezing the model in a finite-element solver.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on six 2D bluff-body wakes at Re=10^4 and evaluated in-sample plus leave-one-shape-out tests; all outperformed steady SST k-ω, and the force model achieved the lowest out-of-sample mean-velocity and drag error (~8.5% drag).
watch_item: Generalization still depends on stable solver deployment and may be sensitive to the chosen regularization and the quality/coverage of the training geometries.
paper_title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
